checkpoints.description: record the bswap 48-round verdict and the all-case verdict pending a quiet window

[1/1] record the bswap measurement that ADR-111 promised: the full 23-case paired run aborted on a hex_io C-twin timeout under concurrent host load, so the paired tool was run over the bswap case alone for 48 interleaved rounds, returning c=0.388 tie, cpp=1.133 tie and rust=1.174 tie in a 0.285-1.204 control band; bswap shipped inline so no pre/post A/B applies; the all-case ALL WON read stays pending a quiet window

impact_assessment.why: ADR-111 ended with the authoritative 48-round verdict and A/B as the next measurement step, and the bswap decision (keep or change the lowering) needs that evidence recorded in the ADR and ledger
impact_assessment.benefits: the bswap case has an interleaved 48-round verdict on the record, the ADR no longer leaves the measurement dangling, and the outstanding full-registry re-run is named explicitly
impact_assessment.risks: contract: documentation and ledger only, no code or benchmark number changes; dependency: none; concurrency: the measurement was taken under concurrent host load, so the wide control band is recorded rather than hidden; state: ledger gains one completion record
impact_assessment.mitigation: record the exact ratios and the aborted full-run condition; do not claim an all-case ALL WON; the paired tool remains unchanged for a quiet-window re-run

checkpoints.description: [1/2] failing-first: the paired verdict drops a baseline whose run times out instead of aborting the whole case, and a lost control pair reports the case as unavailable; [2/2] ADR-113, suite and gates, commit, then run the 23-case 48-round verdict in the background and record it

impact_assessment.why: the authoritative 23-case paired run aborted mid-run when hex_io's portable C twin, normally 5-7 s, hit the 120 s per-run timeout under concurrent host load; one slow baseline discarded eleven cases that had already measured cleanly
impact_assessment.benefits: a case with one unavailable baseline still reports verdicts for the remaining languages, so a single timeout no longer voids an entire authoritative verdict run under load
impact_assessment.risks: contract: measure_interleaved may omit a timed-out key and verdicts_from_samples returns no band when the control pair is incomplete; callers are measure_case and main only; dependency: none new, subprocess.TimeoutExpired is already raised by timed(); concurrency: each key is guarded independently inside the interleaved round, so other keys keep their samples; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests pin the dropped key and the missing-control result; the existing order and spike-cancellation tests must stay green; full suite and project gates before the commit
